proof:
The equation $A(z,x)=s$ determines the component of $x$ parallel to $c$. The remaining component is uniquely $Ey$ because $E$ is an isometry onto $c^\perp$. Thus $F$ is an affine bijection onto the level plane, keeps the integer base, and is an isometry on each fixed-base continuous fiber. This proves the fiber measure identity, with counting measure when $N=0$. A closed ambient halfspace containing a slice point restricts to a closed halfspace in the chart or the whole chart if its functional is constant there. Conversely a proper chart halfspace is the restriction of an ambient halfspace by extending its affine functional from the level plane. The whole-chart option has full mass and cannot lower the infimum, with depth given by full mass in a zero-dimensional chart. These facts give equality of depths.

The sampled hull $K=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times D'_z)$ is compact because the union is finite and compact. It lies inside the convex set $D'$ and contains each listed fiber, so the listed fibers are exact. Its projection is $\operatorname{conv}P$. Every integer point of that projection admits a convex combination of sample bases, with an actual point of $K$ over it obtained by choosing one point in each contributing fiber. It therefore belongs to $P$. As $M>0$, one fiber supplies all $N$ vertical directions, and projected differences supply $k$ independent base directions. Since $K$ lies in $\operatorname{aff}P\times\mathbb R^N$, its dimension is exactly $k+N$.

Translate the base by a point of $P$ and use a lattice basis of $\operatorname{span}(P-P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. This intersection is discrete and contains $k$ linearly independent integer differences, so it is a full-rank lattice in the direction space and contains precisely the ambient lattice differences in that space. Its basis gives all the integer points of the affine base space in standard $\mathbb Z^k$ coordinates. The continuous coordinate is unchanged. Restricting and extending halfspaces between the affine hull and its containing chart has the same full-or-proper trace convention as above, so depth is preserved. The hull is full dimensional in this chart, and retains all nonempty boundary fibers.

For $k,N\ge1$ the hypothesized sharp lower-continuous-dimension theorem applies to this full-dimensional body with mixed measure $M$. For $k=0<N$ the full-mass centroid case of 6769574fc1bd9f8d gives $\Gamma_N M$ on its only fiber. For $N=0<k$, apply the mixed-lattice consequence of 6d6fcf377e68c79c in dimensions $(k,0)$ to the counting measure. It gives depth at least $2^{-k}M$ at an integer point. That point must belong to the sampled hull, since strict separation of any point outside the hull gives a containing halfspace of zero mass. When $k=N=0$ the unique point has mass $M$. Transport the selected point through both charts. Every containing ambient closed halfspace has the same trace mass, and $k\le n$ gives the weaker bound. Common positive scalar weights multiply each cap mass and the total by the same factor.
statement:
Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex with $d\ge1$, let $A(z,x)=a+b\cdot z+c\cdot x$ with $c\ne0$, and fix $s\in\mathbb R$. Put $N=d-1$ and $T=D\cap\{A=s\}\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. For a linear isometry $E:\mathbb R^N\to c^\perp$ use
$$
F(z,y)=\left(z,\frac{s-a-b\cdot z}{\|c\|^2}c+Ey\right),\qquad D'=F^{-1}(D\cap\{A=s\}).
$$
This chart preserves all fiber $\mathcal H_N$ measures and both raw and, for positive total measure, normalized closed-halfspace depths.

Suppose the slice measure $M=\sum_z\mathcal H_N(T_z)$ is positive. Let $P$ be every nonempty integer base of $D'$, including zero-volume fibers, and $k=\dim\operatorname{aff}P$. The hull of the sampled fibers of $D'$ has exactly those integer fibers and is a compact convex body in a saturated affine lattice chart of dimensions $(k,N)$. It preserves the slice measure and all closed-halfspace depths under the charts.

If the sharp mixed center bound in continuous dimension $N$ is available for every positive integer dimension, one point of $T$ lies in no closed ambient halfspace of slice mass less than $2^{-k}\Gamma_NM\ge2^{-n}\Gamma_NM$, where $\Gamma_N=(N/(N+1))^N$ for $N\ge1$ and $\Gamma_0=1$. The cases with $N=0$ or $k=0$ use counting measure or the ordinary centroid bound, respectively. Multiplying all fiber masses by a common positive inverse-coarea factor preserves normalized depths.
title: An actual affine level slice is a lower-continuous-dimensional mixed body
